correctness.rationale: For a row of largest squared norm ell and a perpendicular unit vector, the sum of squared perpendicular projections of the other rows is exactly 1. Some pair has Gram determinant ell p with p>=1/(N-1) and trace at most 2 ell; determinant divided by trace bounds its lesser eigenvalue from below. Thus every E optimizer is invertible with sigma_min squared at least 1/[2(N-1)], including N=2, and deleting rows gives sigma_max<=1. In the witness, with t^2=1/(4N-11), the two axis squared sums are both (4N-11)t^2. A nonsingular pair uses both axes, and only pairing the largest horizontal row with a height-2t vertical row attains 2t for sigma_min. All N-3 such choices have kappa squared N-3, while the two height/width-t rows give condition 1. Since all condition numbers are at least 1, this proves the order of the worst multiplicative gap. Independently reproduced by exact rational enumeration for N=5 through 100 (`python3 repro_record1.py`); did not run the supplied checker. The algebra, not the replay, covers all N.

evidence: A max-volume pair B expresses U as ZB, with identity on the selected rows and every entry in each remaining row of Z bounded by 1 in modulus (single-row determinant swaps). Thus ||Z||²<=1+2(N-2), and orthonormality implies the established max-volume approach already yields the stronger inverse-norm bound sqrt(2N-3), which transfers to all E maximizers.

value.rationale: It rigorously quantifies how badly a legitimate stability objective can do for a different, scale-invariant objective, even for all ties in the global E optimum. A matching-order explicit witness with K optimum 1 is useful for analyzing unweighted two-row sketches. It illustrates the difference between preserving absolute lengths and minimizing norm distortion, without claiming that conditioning alone controls solver errors or that the example extends to uniform leverage.
